summary: Per-material reference surface reflectance (physical albedo) and the on-screen sRGB bands those albedos must land in at the fixed noon calibration capture, AFTER the exposure-chain root fix (sun COLOR -> IRRADIANCE, x PI). The bands are derived by running the measured texture linear-albedo through the real lighting_pass.frag chain at noon and allowing a tolerance for normal/roughness variation and RGBA8 quantization. These are ABSOLUTE bands: a render that is globally too dark (the pre-fix defect) fails them even though relative ordering passes.

exposure_audit.chain: ambient(sky*albedo*ao) + sunDiffuse(kD*albedo/PI * sunRadiance * NdotL) + spec -> ACES filmic -> gamma 1/2.2
exposure_audit.root_cause: Diffuse divides albedo by PI but sun radiance was the raw unit-ish sun COLOR (~1.0), not surface IRRADIANCE (~PI). The unmatched 1/PI division darkened every lit surface by ~PI (3.14x). An 18% gray plate landed at on-screen sRGB ~0.32 instead of perceptual mid (~0.50); a white plate could not exceed ~0.74; sand read rust-brown and grass near-black.
exposure_audit.fix: lighting_pass.frag: sunRadiance = u_sun.color * SUN_IRRADIANCE_SCALE, SUN_IRRADIANCE_SCALE = PI. Applied to the SUN only (point lights carry explicit intensity; ambient is already an irradiance term). Documented in-shader.
exposure_audit.geometry_note: Representative on-flat-ground noon geometry used for band derivation: N=+Z, V=+Z (NdotV=1), L tilted (NdotL=0.85), no specular singularity. The headless gate uses two tilted suns; bands are widened to cover both and the normal-mapped shading spread.

reference_sources: Dry/light sand quartz albedo ~0.30-0.45 (Tetzlaff 1983; Oke, Boundary Layer Climates, surface albedo tables).

Green grass / short vegetation broadband albedo ~0.16-0.26 visible-band; physical leaf albedo low (chlorophyll absorbs R+B), perceptually rendered brighter than its photometric luminance. (Oke 1987; Monteith & Unsworth, Principles of Environmental Physics).
Bare soil albedo ~0.10-0.20, darker when moist (Oke 1987 surface albedo tables).
Granite / light stone albedo ~0.20-0.35; dark igneous rock (basalt/dark gravel) ~0.05-0.15 (USGS spectral library; engineering surface reflectance references).
Deepslate / dark gravel: dark stone end, linear luminance ~0.08-0.15.

materials.name: Stone
materials.note: AmbientCG Rock028 is a darker grey rock (lin lum 0.083) at the dark-granite/basalt end; kept as measured (photographic albedo) rather than brightened.

materials.name: Grass
materials.note: Physically dark (chlorophyll); green channel must dominate. Rendered green and readable after fix, not near-black.

materials.name: Sand
materials.note: Dry sand, squarely in reference band. Brightest plate. Renders warm tan after fix, not rust-brown.

relative_ordering_retained: Sand is the brightest plate (sand_luma > grass_luma).
Grass green channel exceeds its blue channel.
